chunks: 2255 - And the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said:

"There are four whose supplication is not rejected until the gates of heaven are opened for them and it reaches the Throne: the supplication of a parent for his child, the wronged person against the one who wronged him, the one performing 'Umrah until he returns, and the fasting person until he breaks his fast."

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ السَّمَاءِ: the gates of heaven; an expression of acceptance and elevation of du'a
key_terms.الصَّائِمِ: the fasting person; one observing sawm (fasting)
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne; indicating the highest degree of nearness and acceptance
key_terms.الْمَظْلُومِ: the wronged person; one who has suffered injustice
key_terms.الْوَالِدِ: the parent; whose supplication for the child is especially answered
key_terms.دَعْوَةٌ: supplication; a prayerful appeal made to Allah

ai.seo_question: Whose supplications are not rejected according to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله؟
ai.summary: This hadith identifies four especially answered supplications and emphasizes the elevated status of their du'a before Allah. It highlights the spiritual force of parental concern, the plea of the oppressed, and the worship-linked du'a of the mu'tamir and the fasting person.
